items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: like what we know today as a Erroll Garner

ctx.x: Well, we had a little breather, session. That's beautiful, man, you have some beautiful advice there. I think we can just about close this drum section. You just happened to mention to me that we hadn't mentioned Chick Webb...

Well, you know they always say the first should be last, the last should be first. Speaking about Chick Webb, I don't speak of Chick Webb the drummer. I speak of Chick Webb the epitomé. You see, with all the phases that we have to play in, music, we're strictly in the contributing phases of the jazz idiom. Now, Mr. Chick Webb's sense of timing - he didn't settle for nothing but the best. Mr. Chick Webb would get one arrangement but he also had two more arrangements.
